analysis: Aminoglycosides are known to be ototoxic and primarily affect hair cells in the cochlea, with a significant impact on the inner hair cells located in the basal area. The consensus in the medical literature indicates that these inner hair cells are particularly vulnerable to damage from aminoglycosides due to their critical role in auditory transduction. While outer hair cells are also affected, the inner hair cells in the basal area are more susceptible to aminoglycoside-induced ototoxicity. Therefore, the best-supported option is that aminoglycosides affect inner hair cells in the basal area.
